speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have a pruritic rash on your bilateral upper extremities; to begin our assessment, how long have you had this rash, and have you noticed any new exposures to plants, chemicals, or new soaps? Additionally, are there any other symptoms accompanying the itching, such as fever, joint pain, or difficulty breathing?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient complains of a pruritic rash on both upper extremities that has been present for 5 months. She notes that the rash occasionally worsens but has not completely resolved at any point. She denies any recent illnesses and mentions that she has not started any new medications or come into contact with any new substances that she is aware of.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Pityriasis Rosea. The 5-month duration of a pruritic rash on the upper extremities without resolving and without obvious triggers is highly suggestive of this condition, often characterized by a "herald patch" followed by a generalized eruption in a "Christmas tree" distribution on the trunk, which may eventually involve the extremities.
